features.quote: about 80 m to the east a lime pit
features.subtype: lime pit (Heb. bor sid), 3.8 m diam., 1.5 m deep, stone-lined

features.quote: three caves, two of which apparently served for burial
features.subtype: two caves apparently used for burial ('tombs' on Fig. 2)

features.quote: one of which was almost completely blocked with earth
features.subtype: cave (third of the three caves, not said to be a burial)

features.quote: water cisterns, one of which has three openings
features.subtype: water cisterns (two 'bor mayim' symbols on Fig. 2); trough beside one opening

date.basis: not dated; the summary says installations around the farmhouses are 'most of them' Byzantine, which does not date these securely

notes: Text p. 159: lime pit 80 m east of the farm; the caves (two used for burial) and the cisterns lie in the area between the lime pit and the farm buildings, i.e. east of the site; positions coded as words E from the unit. Fig. 2 (p. 160) has a half-arrow north pointing to the upper right (about 58 deg clockwise from page-up) and a 0-20 m bar; on it the cisterns and 'tombs' lie roughly ENE-E of Building I, consistent with the text. No plan position used: the unit point (177900/139400, 100 m precision; the article's map ref 17790/13940 is the same point) cannot be placed on the plan, which has no grid. Not coded: the plastered winepress collecting vat in Building I (a vat, Phase B Byzantine), the trough, quarries. Fig. 1 is a location map with 1-km grid values, no north arrow or scale, and shows no pit, pool or grave. The separate farmhouse in Area A (~300 m NW) is not in the excerpt. No mouth relation is stated.
